name: Ladder Of Abstraction Rubric
description: Evaluation criteria for a ladder-of-abstraction audit: rung tagging, run-rule enforcement, trap repair by climbing down, gap honesty, top-rung discipline, and readability routing

criteria.name: Rung Tagging Completeness
criteria.description: Whether every paragraph or beat carries exactly one rung tag, with R1 pointers recorded for R3 and R4 claims

scores.1: No tagging performed; the audit reasons about the draft impressionistically
scores.2: Partial tagging; some paragraphs untagged or left ambiguous, which is treated as acceptable
scores.3: Every paragraph tagged, but R3/R4 claims carry no pointer to the R1 evidence beneath them
scores.4: Every paragraph tagged with one rung, R1 pointers recorded for most R3/R4 claims, rung map produced as a table
scores.5: Complete rung map with pointers on every R3/R4 claim, ambiguous cases forced to a decision with the reason noted, and costume-R1 paragraphs correctly demoted

criteria.name: Run-Rule Enforcement
criteria.description: Whether the six run rules were applied and every violation reported with its paragraph range before any repair was attempted

scores.1: No run rules applied; the draft is edited paragraph by paragraph on feel
scores.2: One or two rules applied informally; violations fixed as encountered, creating new traps downstream
scores.3: Most rules applied; violation list produced but incomplete or missing paragraph ranges
scores.4: All six rules applied, full violation list with ranges and rule numbers, produced before repairs began
scores.5: All six rules applied with the middle-share computation, plus a sawtooth check confirming the alternation is a run constraint rather than a metronome

criteria.name: Trap Repair By Climbing Down
criteria.description: Whether middle-rung traps were repaired with a real particular from the material rather than by simplifying vocabulary

scores.1: Traps fixed by synonym substitution or by shortening sentences; the paragraph is simpler and just as unintelligible
scores.2: Some concrete language added, but it is generic or analogical rather than a specific instance from the record
scores.3: Real particulars supplied for most traps, though some repairs still rely on plainer jargon
scores.4: Every repaired trap gained a named particular traceable to the material, with the repair type labelled
scores.5: Every repair traceable to a source, checked for representativeness, with extreme cases flagged as extreme when used in load-bearing positions

criteria.name: Fabrication Resistance and Gap Honesty
criteria.description: Whether missing particulars produced gap entries rather than plausible invented specifics, and whether persistent gaps escalated

scores.1: Invented dates, names, numbers, or scenes appear in the repaired prose; nothing distinguishes them from sourced material
scores.2: Composite or 'typical' examples used to fill gaps, presented as if particular
scores.3: No fabrication, but missing particulars are silently left as abstraction with no gap entry recorded
scores.4: Gap log produced with mechanism, artifact sought, and where searched, for every unfillable trap
scores.5: Complete gap log plus explicit escalation when a section accumulates three or more gaps, stating that the defect is missing material rather than missing prose

criteria.name: Top-Rung Discipline
criteria.description: Whether the ceiling was declared from the material in advance, and whether every R4 claim passed the counter-sentence test and the generic test

scores.1: Piece crowned with a universal significance the material does not support; no ceiling declared and no test run
scores.2: Ceiling declared only after drafting, or R4 claims softened with hedges instead of deleted
scores.3: Ceiling declared; generic test run but counter-sentences either missing or written weak so the claim survives
scores.4: Ceiling declared from the material before drafting, counter-sentence written for every R4, generic claims cut or dropped one rung
scores.5: All of level 4, plus counter-sentences recorded in the output as receipts, and material with several independent findings given separate ascents instead of one strained abstraction

criteria.name: Readability Routing Integrity
criteria.description: Whether failing readability scores were classified (a) split, (b) middle-rung trap, or (c) necessary term before editing, and whether meaning survived

scores.1: Score optimized directly: sentences chopped and precise terms swapped for vaguer ones until the number passed
scores.2: Some diagnosis attempted, but qualifiers deleted or causal links severed to shorten sentences
scores.3: Fixes classified, but no meaning-diff performed after repair
scores.4: Every failing paragraph classified before editing, forbidden fixes avoided, meaning diffed after each repair
scores.5: All of level 4, plus the fix-class distribution reported, with a (b)-dominated run flagged as a warning sign rather than passed as clean

criteria.name: System-Protagonist Handling
criteria.description: Whether the technique was applied correctly when the protagonist is a market, protocol, institution, codebase, or supply chain

scores.1: System granted wants, decisions, and beliefs throughout; intentional verbs assert causation the analysis never established
scores.2: Some anthropomorphism repaired, but the repairs produced agentless passives that obscure causation further
scores.3: Intentional verbs largely repaired; R1 rung filled with generalized description rather than dated, instrumented particulars
scores.4: Agency relocated onto actors, mechanisms, or selection pressures; R1 supplied by first-detection events with timestamps and units
scores.5: All of level 4, with agentless-passive count checked after the pass, at most one flagged personification per section, and the mechanism it stands in for named

criteria.name: Scaffolding Invisibility
criteria.description: Whether the planning apparatus was removed from the delivered prose

scores.1: Rung labels, altitude vocabulary, and section roadmaps appear in the prose; it reads as an outline that learned to talk
scores.2: Explicit signposting throughout ('zooming out', 'as we saw above', 'at a high level')
scores.3: Most scaffolding removed, some transitional signposting remains
scores.4: No rung vocabulary or roadmap sentences survive; the ladder is invisible to a reader
scores.5: Scaffolding fully absent, the A-frame close lands without a 'which shows that', and a reader could not recite the structure after one read
